actor: core maintainer of a mainstream open agent-RL or post-training library
job: Adding a first-class cached or replayed rollout mode that swaps live multi-turn tool execution for masked offline-trajectory replay in the RL loop.
outcome: A second open RL framework other than CacheRL's own code ships documented, first-class support for cached-replay rollouts for multi-turn tool-calling RL.
motivation: The live-tool-execution tax dominates agent-RL cost for every user of the library, so a drop-in cheaper rollout retains and grows adoption.

task.who: the library's rollout and trainer-loop engineering team
task.what: implement a cached-replay rollout mode with token masking
task.where: TRL, verl, OpenRLHF, SkyRL, ART, or NeMo-RL
task.why: cut the universal live-tool-execution cost their users pay
task.how: offline trajectory replay plus a cache-tier-aware hybrid reward

actor: independent agent-RL research group on a non-CacheRL base model family
job: Reproducing cached-rollout RL on a different base model and releasing open weights or training code with reported tool-calling accuracy and rollout-cost numbers.
outcome: An independent open reproduction lands tool-calling accuracy within ten points of a frontier model at order-of-magnitude-lower rollout cost on a new model.
motivation: A clean cheap reproduction near frontier accuracy is a high-citation, copy-worthy result that establishes the group's method credibility.

task.who: the group's post-training researchers and infrastructure engineers
task.what: reproduce cached-rollout RL and release weights or code
task.where: the group's training cluster and an open model-release hub
task.why: prove the method generalizes beyond the original Qwen3 result
task.how: three-tier fuzzy trajectory cache with token-level masking

actor: maintainer of an inference-coupled rollout or trajectory-logging stack
job: Hardening trajectory capture, fuzzy-cache lookup, and masking primitives so any RL trainer can plug in replayed rollouts instead of calling live tools.
outcome: Reusable cached-replay rollout infrastructure that a downstream RL framework can adopt to ship its own documented cached-rollout training mode.
motivation: Owning the rollout-and-cache layer makes the stack the default substrate for cheap agent-RL and entrenches it across multiple trainers.

task.who: the stack's rollout-engine and serving maintainers
task.what: build cache, lookup, and masking primitives for replayed rollouts
task.where: the inference-coupled rollout engine and its trajectory store
task.why: become the shared substrate that cuts agent-RL rollout cost
task.how: three-tier fuzzy cache, token masking, and trainer-facing APIs
